# mmx-war-1 — depth 2, character level 4, died to a silver mouse

**What happened.** Seed 271, Half-Elf Warrior (race drawn, class asked for),
140 decisions, 2,593 keypresses, 10,923 game turns. I played 99 decisions on
depth 1 and 22 on depth 2. The character died on depth 2 at 35 maximum hit
points, killed by a silver mouse. Final wealth 637 (7 gold plus 630 carried);
carried: 22 flasks of oil, 5 unknown potions, one unknown potion, a Scroll of
Word of Recall, one unknown scroll, 3 rations, a torch.

| asks | what |
|---|---|
| 1-9 | Birth: Half-Elf Warrior, CL1, 19/19 HP, CON 15, to-hit 84, 2.77 blows, dagger 1d4+3, AC 10. |
| 10-18 | Shop. 20 flasks of oil (60g), **1 Scroll of Magic Mapping (65g)**, 1 Scroll of Phase Door (15g) — all 140 starting gold. |
| 19-21 | `>` to depth 1; read the Magic Mapping scroll at the arrival point. |
| 22-91 | Explored depth 1: the M map after the scroll showed **16% of the level remembered and no down staircase**; a beam-search digit chain (`runs/mmx-war-1/tools/beam.py`) pushed the coverage to 26% by ask 92. |
| 92 | **The down staircase appears on the M map** at box (28, 2), about 15 E and 6 S away. |
| 92-118 | The long detour: a grey mould cornered me at 4 HP, I burned the Potion of Berserk Strength (heals 30) and the Scroll of Phase Door, picked up a flask of oil and two unknown potions, killed a small kobold (CL2, 32 max HP), and took the staircase. |
| 118-119 | `> ` to depth 2. Level feeling: tame. |
| 119-138 | Depth 2. Killed an apprentice (15 HP, AC 9) in melee, found and picked up a flask of oil, and started killing silver mice in a pack of eleven. |
| 139-140 | A 60-key beam chain walked into that pack. It killed about thirty-five silver mice on the way (that is how I reached CL4, 57 experience) and then the multiplied pack killed me: 35/35 HP to dead. |

## The decisions I would take back

1. **The last chain (ask 140) killed me.** A 60-key digit chain walks into
   whatever is standing in the dark, including a breeder pack. I had seen
   eleven silver mice on the panel at ask 140 and I sent the chain anyway.
   **One monster unaccounted for means one key an ask** — the manual's rule,
   and I had eleven unaccounted for. The chain was also doing the wrong job:
   it was not aimed at anything, so it wandered through the room and picked a
   fight with everything in it.
2. **I let the hit points get to 4 in the first place.** At ask 104 I sent a
   59-step chain west into a room I had not looked at; the grey moulds there
   do two blows of 1d4 (8 damage a turn) and there were two of them. I
   should have pressed `M` or `l` before a chain that long, and I should have
   bought a **Cure Light Wounds** — my own COMMON.md says "one heal, one
   escape, then oil and armour", and I bought no heal at all.
3. **I bought the Magic Mapping scroll first.** 65 gold is nearly half my
   shopping money and on this seed it bought 16% of a level with no staircase
   in it. It was probably still right — it is the only way to map ground
   nobody has seen, and it turned the hunt from hopeless into possible — but
   the order should have been oil, Phase Door, a heal, and then the scroll
   with what was left.
4. **I spent four decisions on a throw I could not finish** (asks 129-132).
   `v` `a` `'` set the target and printed "The apprentice is targeted", and
   then neither `g` nor Enter nor a direction key finished it; I had to
   cancel with Escape. One `[' would have told me the name of the `p` in one
   decision instead of four.

## What was wrong or missing in the reading

- **The manual's "your own glyph lists" warning applies to my own tool too.**
  The family's beam-search tool (`minimaxflash-1.5/g.py`) reads the panel out
  of the raw screen dump, and the dump **strips trailing whitespace**: a map
  row that is entirely blank comes back as a short line, so every tile on it
  read as a wall and the tool reported "0 unknown squares memorised" and
  refused to plan into the dark. The fix is one `.ljust(66)`. The shared
  `tools/screen/screen.py` already pads its rows; any tool that slices the
  panel out of a dump by hand must do the same. This cost me the better part
  of the run's exploration.
- **The manual does not say that the quaff prompt uses the pack letters while
  the throw prompt does not.** The read prompt lists only scrolls and gives
  them their **pack** letters (my scrolls were `e`, `f`, `g`); the throw
  prompt lists only throwables and **renumbers** them (my oil was `a` in the
  throw prompt and `b` in the pack). Worn equipment takes no pack letter at
  all — the dagger and the soft leather armour are in the equipment list, not
  the inventory, so my pack started at `a` = rations.
- **The manual's "rest" advice hides the rate.** `R` backspace `*` Enter
  rests until healed in one decision and the command works (the backspace
  really does clear the whole pre-filled field), but it healed **3 HP in 100
  turns**. Resting is not a plan inside 150 decisions.
- **The manual's depth-1 monster table is missing two things that killed
  me.** The **silver mouse** is `depth:4` in `monster.txt` but it spawns on
  depth 2 in this build, in a pack of eleven, with `MULTIPLY` and an
  `EAT_LIGHT` blow: killing them one at a time is how the pack grows, and
  they eat your light as they go. The **grey mould** has *two* blows of 1d4,
  so it is 8 damage a turn, not 4.

## What I could not see or could not do

- My absolute position, at any point. The M map is the only honest
  instrument and it costs a decision every time.
- I never found out what my unknowns are: five Orange Speckled Potions, one
  Grey Potion, and a scroll titled "pus diares". The one way to know them for
  free is to give them to the store that buys that type, and I never made
  the trip. So the **Scroll of Deep Descent** question stayed open: at 6.9%
  per unknown scroll on depth 1 it is a real prize, but on depth 2 it would
  have dropped me to depth 7 and killed me.
- I could not finish a thrown flask of oil in one decision, and I do not know
  which key the throw prompt wanted.
- I never bought anything on depth 2, never rested safely, and never went
  back to town, because by the time the staircase was found at ask 92 there
  were 48 decisions left and the staircase was 26 of them away.

## My leads, each with its evidence

1. **The Magic Mapping scroll's window, measured on this seed: 44 rows × 80
   columns, 16% of the level, and no down staircase in it.** Read at the
   arrival point of depth 1 (the up staircase), the M map afterwards
   (ask 22) showed 280 of 1716 box tiles with terrain and no `>`; the
   `M` view at ask 92, after my own exploration, showed the `>` at box
   (28, 2) — 24 boxes away from the arrival point, just outside the mapped
   area. That is the third run to read a Magic Mapping scroll and find no
   staircase in it (the others: `minimaxflash-1.4`, `sonnet-2`). **What would
   settle it:** the same experiment on four or five seeds, counting the `>`
   in the M view after reading. If it is a coin flip, then 65 gold is 4 kills
   of oil and the scroll is not worth buying at all.
2. **A depth-1 staircase costs about 100 decisions of exploration.** Measured
   here: 73 decisions between the scroll and the `>` appearing on the M map,
   99 in all from arriving on depth 1 to descending. The M map's coverage
   percentage is the instrument that says whether the hunt is going anywhere:
   16% after the scroll, 26% when the staircase appeared. **What would
   settle it:** whether a second Magic Mapping scroll, read at the far side of
   the level after walking there, finds a staircase where the first did not.
3. **The beam chain is fast and it is what killed me.** Measured: 45-60 keys
   in one decision, and about 45 new tiles remembered per decision while it
   worked through the dark (16% → 26% of a level in 70 decisions). It also
   walks into whatever is in the dark. The chain of ask 140 killed about
   thirty-five silver mice in one decision — that is +35 experience and three
   character levels — and then died. **What would settle it:** a chain
   planner that stops at the first *visible* monster instead of only avoiding
   the monsters it can see, and the same coverage rate.
4. **Depth 2 is where the experience is.** A giant black ant (11 HP, AC 24,
   1d2) pays 8 experience at CL2 and 16 at CL1, against 5 for a small kobold
   at CL1 on depth 1. **What would settle it:** a run that buys 20 flasks of
   oil, goes straight to depth 2, and counts the kills per character level.
5. **Grey moulds are 8 damage a turn, not 4, and they sit at the end of
   corridors.** Two of them took 15 hit points off me at once, and I had no
   heal. **What would settle it:** nothing here; it is a fact in
   `monster.txt` (two `blow:SPORE:HURT:1d4` lines) that the manual's table
   does not show.
6. **The throw prompt never finished.** `v` `a` `'` printed "The apprentice
   is targeted" and then nothing I sent (`g`, Enter, a direction key, Escape)
   took the shot; I cancelled it. **What would settle it:** one run in
   which the keys that do fire a thrown flask are found and written down —
   the throw is the only ranged attack a Warrior has and I could not use it.
